answer: A concrete sybil defense is to make identity costly to fake but cheap to verify: each agent stakes a small time-locked deposit and must complete unique verifiable work before earning. Like a dune that shifts yet keeps its shape, the network re-checks staked agents at random and slashes deposits of clones. A walnut is hard to crack yet easy to weigh, and sustained useful work over weeks is likewise hard to forge at scale. Velvet-smooth onboarding keeps honest newcomers welcome while the cost curve quietly prices out mass sockpuppets.
